title: Deployment pace & utilization projections (NA / EU / APAC) Q3-Q4 2027
content:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a pragmatic rollout cadence and utilization profile for GPU fleet expansion across NA / EU / APAC for the Q3–Q4 2027 horizon. It is intended to be operational: week-by-week ramp targets, utilization SLOs, throttling thresholds, and actions for each region.

Context and constraints (short):
- We anticipate onboarding two major GPU families across cloud providers in this window (A100-class for high-throughput and an LLM-inference-optimized AmpereXT variant). Procurement lead times and cloud quota approvals vary by region.
- Objective is to increase available token-per-second capacity by ~2.6x from current baseline while keeping steady-state fleet utilization in the 60–75% range to preserve latency SLOs and headroom for sudden surge traffic.
- Preference: staggered region rollout to reduce cross-region supply risk and reuse on-call/ops playbooks between waves.

High-level goals (metrics):
- Target aggregate capacity increase: +160% by end of Q4 2027 vs baseline (measured in peak concurrent generations per minute).
- Desired steady utilization: 60–75% for running fleet at normal customer load.
- Cold-start buffer: maintain 20% buffer capacity for spike absorption without SLA degradation.
- Ramp rollback threshold: if regional P99 latency increases >20% vs baseline for 3 consecutive hours, initiate canary rollback.

Planned rollout waves (recommended):
- Wave A (NA primary): weeks 1–6 of the plan. Focus on AZs with existing quota agreements.
- Wave B (EU primary): weeks 5–12. Overlap with late NA stabilization to reuse SRE muscle memory.
- Wave C (APAC): weeks 10–18. Longer lead-times anticipated (quotas & interconnect testing).

Weekly cadence and sample ramp table (week numbers are relative to plan start):

Week | Region | New GPUs (nodes) | Expected added QPS* | Target util (avg) | Notes
-----|--------|------------------|---------------------|------------------|------
1    | NA     | 40               | +18%                | 30%              | quota uplift in us-east-1, enable auto-batch tuning
2    | NA     | 60               | +28%                | 40%              | enable KV-prefetch on canary pools
3    | NA     | 80               | +36%                | 50%              | ramp routing policy to prefer NA variants for low-latency customers
4    | NA     | 100              | +45%                | 60%              | enable burst capacity for high-tier tenants
5    | NA     | 0                | +0%                 | 62%              | stabilization, validation sweep, begin EU onboarding prep
6    | NA     | 0                | +0%                 | 60%              | run stress tests, SLO check; if green, proceed to Wave B
7    | EU     | 50               | +20%                | 35%              | egress testing and regional KMS check
8    | EU     | 70               | +30%                | 45%              | enable canary traffic split 5%
9    | EU     | 80               | +38%                | 55%              | observability: token-level latency sampling
10   | EU     | 90               | +45%                | 60%              | cross-region fallback validation
11   | EU     | 0                | +0%                 | 60%              | stabilization, run quality/eval checks
12   | EU     | 0                | +0%                 | 58%              | finalize APAC vendor confirmations
13   | APAC   | 30               | +12%                | 30%              | longer procurement lead; initial smoke tests
14   | APAC   | 50               | +22%                | 40%              | enable local KV cache regionally
15   | APAC   | 70               | +34%                | 50%              | connectivity tests to control plane
16   | APAC   | 90               | +44%                | 60%              | late-stage tuning and UAT with select customers
17   | APAC   | 0                | +0%                 | 58%              | stabilization window
18   | APAC   | 0                | +0%                 | 60%              | final validation and streamlining autoscale rules

*Expected added QPS is approximate relative customer-facing throughput; mapping to tokens/sec is in the linked spreadsheet.

Throttle matrix (operational thresholds):
- GREEN: average utilization 50–75%, P95 latency <= baseline + 10%: no action.
- YELLOW: util >75% OR P95 latency baseline + 10–20%: restrict non-critical background jobs, enable aggressive batching, raise customer-tier rate limit thresholds.
- RED: util >85% OR P95 latency > baseline + 20% OR error-rate spike > 0.5%: divert new traffic to fallback model variants, trigger immediate autoscale up if spare quota, or throttle burst customers.

Rollback criteria (canary rollback flow):
- If any canary group shows P99 latency > baseline + 20% for 3 consecutive hours OR customer error reports exceed threshold, run partial rollback to previous fleet configuration (rollback steps captured in runbook RN-67).

Operational playbook highlights (quick checklist):
- Pre-rollout (week -2 to 0): verify quota requests approved, KMS policies in place, test storage/e2e network peering in staging.
- Day-of: coordinate with SRE on-call, freeze non-essential deploys, set alert suppression for noise, publish rollout channel (infra-rollout-waves).
- After each incremental add (per-day): run 30-minute smoke tests for P50/P95 latencies, cross-check cost dashboard for unexpected spend jumps.
- Post-wave (48–72h): run quality evals on sampled traffic (regressions, hallucination rate for generative tasks), update rollout notes.

Cost & utilization forecast snippet (monthly normalized):
- Baseline monthly GPU hours: 280k
- Expected added monthly GPU hours by end of Q4: +190k
- Unit economics target: keep cost-per-1000-tokens within +8% of current baseline by using dynamic batching + prefix cache.

Risks and mitigations (short list):
- Quota delays (APAC): pre-submit cloud quota requests and activate emergency spot+reserved mixing for critical drops.
- Vendor image compatibility: maintain a small compatibility test harness per model family; gate larger rollouts on green harness.
- Cross-region network flakiness impacting KV caching: increase local cache TTLs as fallback and instrument evictions.
- Unexpected hot-tenants: pre-identify top-20 tenants by tokens/min and schedule dedicated capacity lanes or limiters.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we want to frontload more capacity in NA in exchange for a slower EU ramp? Tradeoff: faster NA growth may increase global risk exposure to supplier failures. (Decision: product + infra to sign off by 2026-10-10)
- APAC vendor: choose between 2 vendors with similar price but different provisioning SLAs — need procurement input.
- Should we reserve 10% of added capacity specifically for experimental internal workloads (labs/benchmarks)?

Appendix: quick operational notes and commands
- Typical checklist commands (ops):
  - kubectl apply -f fleet-config-wave-a.yaml --context=infra-na
  - ./scripts/run-smoke --region=eu --schema=latency-sample
  - dashboard links: (confluence id above) and the cost sheet: drive:costs/q4-2027-projection (linked_artifacts)

Meeting cadence for this plan:
- Weekly rollout sync (Mon 09:00 PT) — core infra + SRE + product + QE.
- Bi-weekly vendor sync (Thu 16:00 PT) — procurement + vendor PMs.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is deliberately prescriptive to make operational handoffs simpler. Expect small adjustments after the first NA wave.
- If you have locality-specific constraints (data residency, KMS differences), flag them inline in the doc comments or Slack #infra-rollouts.
